title: A Self-Inverse Rational Function: f(f(x)) = x
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Let f(x) = 2x/(x - 2) on its natural domain. Show that f composed with itself returns the input, f(f(x)) = x, for every admissible x, and identify where the composition is defined.

steps.title: Substitute f into Itself
steps.explanation: Every occurrence of the input in the rule f = 2*(input)/(input - 2) is replaced by the whole fraction 2x/(x - 2).
steps.why: Composition means feeding the output of the inner copy into the outer rule; the substitution is purely mechanical.

steps.title: Clear the Complex Fraction
steps.explanation: The top doubles to 4x/(x-2); the bottom combines over the common denominator x-2, where the 2x terms cancel and leave the constant 4.
steps.why: Writing both tiers over the shared denominator x-2 exposes identical denominators that will cancel in the next division.

steps.title: Divide and Recover x
steps.explanation: Dividing the two tiers cancels the factor 4/(x-2) entirely, collapsing the composition to the identity map.
steps.why: For x != 2 the denominator 4/(x-2) is nonzero, so the division and cancellation are legitimate.

steps.title: Audit the Admissible Inputs
steps.explanation: The inner f requires x != 2; the outer f additionally requires f(x) != 2, but that equation has no solution at all, so x = 2 is the only exclusion. (Checking the coefficient: f(f(x)) = x fails for the similar rule 2x/(x-1), whose composition gives 4x/(x+1).)
steps.why: A double composition of a Mobius map is the identity precisely when its coefficient matrix squares to a scalar multiple of the identity; the domain audit confirms the identity holds everywhere it is defined.
